sections.title: Introduction
sections.extract: Thurston observed that ideal triangulations are a useful tool to study the geometry and topology of cusped hyperbolic 3--manifolds. Geometric triangulations are useful to study geometric properties of a manifold. Minimal triangulations, i.e.topological ideal triangulations using the least number of ideal 3--simplices, are used in census enumeration, and as a platform to study the topology of the manifold using

sections.title: Minimal ideal triangulations via geometry
sections.extract: The canonical cell decompositions of cusped hyperbolic 3--manifolds due to Epstein and Penner [@Epstein-euclidean-1988] are generically ideal triangulations. It follows from work of Guéritaud [@GueritaudPhDThesis Theorem 2.1.7 in Section 2.1.4] that the canonical cell decompositions of hyperbolic 2--bridge link complements are ideal triangulations. However, these are not minimal in general. We thank Jessica Purcell

sections.title: Minimal ideal triangulations via topology
sections.extract: In this paper, we are first concerned with the anatomy of a minimal ideal triangulation. In particular, in §[\[sec:anatomy\]](#sec:anatomy){reference-type="ref" reference="sec:anatomy"} we characterise edges of low degree, and analyse subcomplexes that we call *maximal layered $\partial$--punctured solid tori.* These are solid tori with a point missing on the boundary, and imbued with a special ideal triangulation.

sections.title: Other classes of hyperbolic 3–manifolds
sections.extract: We remark that for closed hyperbolic 3--manifolds, currently no infinite families of minimal triangulations are known. In the case of compact manifolds with non-empty boundary, lower bounds on complexity are known through work of [@Bucher-simplicial-2015] and [@Jaco-bounds-2016], where it is independently shown that they are attained by $S_g\times[0,1],$ where $S_g$ is a closed orientable surface of genus $g\ge 1.$

sections.extract: []{#sec:lst label="sec:lst"} A *layered solid torus* $\operatorname{LST}$ is a triangulation of a solid torus iteratively constructed in the following way: Start with a one-triangle Möbius strip as shown in Figure [\[fig:faces\]](#fig:faces){reference-type="ref" reference="fig:faces"}(c). Then attach additional tetrahedra without a twist along pairs of (unpaired) faces of the existing complex sharing an edge $e$.

sections.title: Properties of minimal triangulations
sections.extract: An ideal triangulation of a topologically finite 3--manifold $M$ is *minimal* if it uses the smallest number of simplices in an ideal triangulation of $M.$ The number of ideal simplices in a minimal ideal triangulation of $M$ is denoted $c(M)$ and termed the *complexity* of $M.$ We assume that the reader is familiar with normal surface theory. sections.title: Low degree edges in minimal ideal triangulations
sections.extract: We now show that there are no edges of degree one or two in a minimal triangulation of a cusped hyperbolic 3--manifold, and that edges of degree three must be contained in layered $\partial$--punctured solid tori. ::: lemma []{#thm:degone label="thm:degone"} If $\mathcal{T}$ is a minimal ideal triangulation of a cusped hyperbolic 3--manifold $M,$ then $\mathcal{T}$ has no edge of degree one. ::: ::: proof *Proof.*
